title: He grew (Luke 2:41–52)
hook: Jesus advanced in wisdom and age and grace

segments.voice: Yesterday, Simeon held the child and asked to be let go in peace. Your line was in peace. What did your eyes see that was worth seeing? Day four hundred forty-eight, the end of the week.

Every parent's nightmare, in five verses. Every year Mary and Joseph go up to Jerusalem for the Passover, and when Jesus is twelve they go as usual. The feast ends. They start home in a big caravan of relatives and neighbors, and they assume he's somewhere in the crowd, with cousins. A whole day's walk later, they look for him. He isn't there. They turn back to Jerusalem, a city packed with pilgrims, and they search. One day. Two days. On the third day, they find him.
screen: `TWELVE YEARS OLD, AT THE PASSOVER.` → `A DAY'S WALK BEFORE THEY NOTICE.` → `THREE DAYS OF SEARCHING.`

segments.voice: He's in the Temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions, and everyone who hears him is astonished at his understanding and his answers. His parents are astonished too, but not in the same way. Mary says what any mother would, in the Douay-Rheims: "Son, why hast thou done so to us? behold thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." And his answer is the first thing Jesus ever says in Luke's Gospel: "How is it that you sought me? did you not know, that I must be about my father's business?" The Greek is short and open: literally, in the things of my Father. It could mean my Father's business, or my Father's house. Translations go both ways. And Luke says plainly: they understood not the word. But here's what happens next. He goes down with them to Nazareth, and is subject to them. Obedient. The boy who knows who his Father is goes home and does what his parents say. Then Luke's summary: "And Jesus advanced in wisdom, and age, and grace with God and men." Advanced. Grew. The Greek word for age, helikia, can also mean stature, so the King James says stature, the Douay says age; both are in it. The Church teaches that the Son of God, being truly human, truly grew: learned to walk, to read, to work with wood, grew in wisdom. Catholics pray this scene as the fifth Joyful Mystery. And it's the last we hear of him for about eighteen years. That closes this week, and Luke's first two chapters: an orderly account, Zachary's silence, the Ave, the Benedictus, Bethlehem, Simeon, and a boy who grew.
screen: `FOUND AMONG THE TEACHERS.` · `MY FATHER'S BUSINESS, OR HOUSE?` · `HE WENT DOWN, AND WAS SUBJECT TO THEM.` · `HELIKIA: AGE, AND STATURE.` · then, large: `JESUS ADVANCED IN WISDOM, AND AGE, AND GRACE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: notice how you've grown. Settle, and breathe. Think back to yourself a year ago, or five years ago. What did you not know then that you know now? Where are you kinder, or braver, or more patient? Take Luke's three words one at a time. Wisdom: something you understand better now. Age: the years themselves, the body that carried you here. Grace: a way you've been given more than you earned. Don't grade yourself. Just notice the growth, even if it's small, even if it came through something hard. If you pray, you can thank God for it. The bell holds the time.
He grew. Luke's words about the boy Jesus after the Temple: he advanced in wisdom, and age, and grace with God and men. Today's word.
Your line: growing is holy. Today, tell someone one way you've seen them grow. Day four hundred forty-eight.

howItsDone: Catholics pray the finding of Jesus in the Temple as the fifth Joyful Mystery of the rosary, and hear this Gospel on the feast of the Holy Family after Christmas.

fork.setup: you're Mary. after three days of searching, you find your twelve-year-old calmly talking with the teachers in the Temple. what do you say?

fork.reveal: "behold thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." and he answers with a question about his Father's business.

original.note: Greek: age, or stature. Luke 2:52: the Douay says age, the King James says stature.

trapdoor: what you thought: a story about a precocious boy.
what it means: a frightened search, a boy who knows his Father, an obedient return home, and a Son of God who truly grew.
what a scholar hears: en tois tou patros mou, in the things of my Father, house or business; helikia, age or stature; and Jesus' first words in Luke.

notes: Douay-Rheims wording of Luke 2:48, 2:49 and 2:52 quoted from memory; please check.
'The first thing Jesus ever says in Luke's Gospel': confirm (no earlier speech by Jesus in Luke 1–2).
CCC 472 on Christ's human knowledge growing; CCC 534 on the finding in the Temple. Confirm the summary 'truly grew... grew in wisdom'.
'About eighteen years' from age twelve to about thirty (Luke 3:23). Confirm.
